items.vms: Cross-node $ENQ grant / block-then-grant / blocking-AST delivered on the mastering node + real holder
items.verified_against: tests/qemu/test_syssvc_dlm_xnode.c (x86_64 + Alpha LP64) — scenario 5 (H5: block-then-grant + deferred-grant report) and scenario 7 (H6: BLKAST wire + holder-side receive) driven against a real /dev/vms executive. (The former two-node run_dlm_harness_h5.sh/_h6.sh QEMU harnesses were retired with the userspace SCSD daemon in the executive-resident pivot, #1052; the receive-handler behavior they proved is now exercised by this injected-cross-node-request test on real /dev/vms.)
items.notes: vms-94c/vms-e8f1/vms-904c + BLKAST wire H6 (vms-76d/#918). vms_lock_dlm_xnode_dispatch runs a decoded cross-node $ENQ through the real lock manager on the mastering node, held FOR the remote requester's CSID: a compatible request GRANTS (SS$_NORMAL, GET_RESMASTER shows held_for=<peer>); an incompatible one QUEUES on the real waiting queue (VMS_DLM_STS_QUEUED, GETLKI shows granted NL / requested EX) and the master fires the blocking-AST decision. The BLKAST is now DELIVERED over SCS and fires a genuine user-mode AST on the remote holder's process (H6, was deferred); a cross-node $DEQ (vms_lock_dlm_xnode_deq, authorized by CSID) releases and grants the blocked request (GETLKI flips NL->EX). Exercised on real /dev/vms single-node with an injected cross-node CSID (tests/qemu/test_syssvc_dlm_xnode.c x86_64 + Alpha LP64); the two-node H5/H6 QEMU harnesses that proved the over-the-wire path were retired in #1052 — multi-node runtime proof pending (vms-1ee). RE-ESTABLISHED 2-node (#1174, tests/lab/captures/xnode-dlm-2node-20260911.log): a live two-node cluster proves cross-node $ENQ->GRANT bidirectionally (each node granted EX by the PEER master, granted_mode=5, grants_received=1) and never-crash-a-peer (both survive the peer's frames, projections=agree) — the first real multi-node proof since the #1052 retirement, partially discharging the vms-1ee caveat for the acquire/grant path. NOW FULLY DISCHARGED for the acquire/grant/notify/release lifecycle (vms-c72 receive arm #1181 + round-trip lab proof #1183, tests/lab/captures/xnode-dlm-2node-resmaster-clean-20260911.log): the receive arm routes inbound op-03 ($DEQ) -> master-side release and op-04 (BLKAST) -> a real user-mode AST on the remote holder, and a live 2-node run proves the FULL emit->receive->deliver round-trip: blkasts_received>0 + blkasts_delivered>0 (BLKAST really delivered, not just emitted, superseding the earlier single-node-injection-only note), and a DIRECT master-side release readback — on node B (master) the granted queue goes n_granted 1->0 with remote_holder cleared AFTER B processes A's inbound $DEQ (counter_rose=1 gates the sample to post-processing), the resource still present (found=1): the LKB actually left the master's granted queue, a lock-DB STATE delta, not a return code. Composed with the in-process assertion (test_dlm_recv_arm: master copy GONE, real engine) this answers return-value!=state at both the unit and live 2-node levels. Only remaster/LVB + distributed-deadlock stay deferred (cluster-dlm$remaster-lvb-deadlock, vms-727). No fake grants OR blocks — a queued request is a real lock on the master's queue that releases only on a real $DEQ (INV-6).

items.vms: Async DLM replies (queued-reply + deferred GRANT) delivered over SCS; requester-side completion
items.verified_against: tests/qemu/test_syssvc_dlm_xnode.c — scenario 5 (H5: the block-then-grant $DEQ REPORTS the flipped waiter so the daemon can wire a deferred GRANT) and scenario 5b (the requester-side VMS_DLM_OP_GRANT receive completes an executive-resident origin record — a queued-reply leaves it NL-pending, a deferred GRANT flips NL->EX, read back on the requester by GETLKI), driven against a real /dev/vms executive. (The former two-node A<->B run_dlm_harness_h5.sh daemon harness — SCSD-I-DLMPEND/DLMDEFER/DLMH5FLIP — was retired with the userspace SCSD daemon in the executive-resident pivot, #1052.)
items.notes: vms-6ca rung H5. The master's async replies ride the live SCS wire: node B WIREs the queued-reply (granted mode NL — the requester stays genuinely pending) and, on a real cross-node $DEQ that flips a queued waiter to granted, WIREs an unprompted deferred GRANT (SS$_NORMAL, the granted mode) to that requester (vms_lock_dlm_xnode_deq reports the flipped waiter). The REQUESTER-SIDE GRANT RECEIVE (VMS_DLM_OP_GRANT) completes an executive-resident ORIGIN record on the requesting node, whose granted mode is set ONLY from what the master sent over SCS; GETLKI reads the NL->EX flip back on the REQUESTER. This origin record is the requester-side wait-for state H11's distributed deadlock search reads (VMS_IOCTL_DLM_ENUM_WAITS). The requester-side receive is exercised single-node on real /dev/vms (tests/qemu/test_syssvc_dlm_xnode.c, injected CSID); the former two-node A<->B run_dlm_harness_h5.sh proof (SCSD-I-DLMPEND/DLMDEFER/DLMH5FLIP) was retired in #1052 — multi-node wire proof pending (vms-1ee). RE-ESTABLISHED 2-node (#1174, tests/lab/captures/xnode-dlm-2node-20260911.log): the async GRANT-reply crosses the live wire and completes on the requester (grants_received=1 on both nodes, NL->EX read back on the real 2-node cluster) — partially discharging vms-1ee for the grant-reply path. NOW FULLY DISCHARGED: the receive arm (vms-c72, #1181) routes the inbound op-03 $DEQ (emit reachable since #1178) to the master-side release and the op-04 BLKAST to a real user-mode AST, and the live 2-node round-trip (#1183) shows the async replies delivered end-to-end — blkasts_delivered>0 and the inbound $DEQ empties the master's granted queue n_granted 1->0 (direct resmaster readback, counter_rose=1 gated). The full async emit->receive->deliver wire is proven 2-node, not just the grant-reply half. No fabricated wire reply or grant (INV-6).

items.vms: LVB replication, dynamic remastering (directory + lock state), directory-ownership guard, distributed deadlock detection
items.verified_against: PARTIAL coverage only — host units tests/cluster/host/test_dlm_ldwv.c (LVB read + wait-for visibility, injected/fake master) + tests/cluster/host/test_dlm_requester.c; N-node simulator scenarios tests/cluster/sim/scenarios/dlm_directory.c (directory routing) + tests/cluster/sim/scenarios/dlm_requester.c (simulated peers); tests/cluster/host/test_codec_dlm.c (REBUILD/DLKSRCH frame codec). The multi-node real-/dev/vms proofs (run_dlm_harness_h8/_h9/_h10/_h10b/_e84/_ec75.sh — LVB write/read crossing, dynamic remaster, directory-ownership refusal, distributed deadlock) were RETIRED with the userspace SCSD daemon in the #1052 executive-resident pivot; their gated multi-node successor through the now-landed SCS arm is still being re-established (vms-1ee; see the 2026-09-14 UPDATE below) — status stays verified->implemented pending that re-established proof. PROGRESS (rd vms-1ee): blocker 1 of 3 CLEARED. The Lock Directory Weight Vector now builds on a real multi-node cluster: when NO peer has advertised a LOCKDIRWT (none can -- no wire byte is pinned for a remote system, FC-P3.2) the local node WITHHOLDS its own SYSGEN weight so p. 6-32's all-zero reading applies cluster-wide, which is the one directory every node computes identically. Gated: the fallback is refused the instant ANY PEER advertises a real weight (split-brain: an all-zero answer to a peer computing a weighted vector is two directories for one resource). Proven on the live 2-node rig -- both executives now report the vector built on the unadvertised reading, where every previous run reported it not rebuilt (tests/qemu/captures/ldwv-fallback-20260911.log); teeth in tests/cluster/host/test_dlm_ldwv.c (club_local_withhold_builds_when_peers_unknown + club_local_withhold_refused_when_a_peer_advertised). Before this, an inbound cross-node $ENQ for a tree this node does not master returned SS$_UNSUPPORTED with no further information, so the requester learned nothing and could only re-resolve blind. The engine now ANSWERS it: when the executive holds the tree's master CSID it replies VMS_DLM_STS_REDIRECT with master_csid set to that node — the book's outcome 2 — and the requester's already-shipping redirect handler (vms_dlm_scs_fsm.c h_redirect) re-addresses. IT IS A REPLY, NEVER A FORWARD. That is the termination argument: exactly one node answers, so no chain of nodes can form and no cycle can be entered. Three responder guards close the single hop: no master held -> decline; target is this node -> decline; target is the REQUESTER -> decline (that answer would bounce the request straight back). The requester's own DLM_REQ_MAX_REDIRECTS budget bounds the exchange from the other end. INV-6: the CSID named is read off the resource block at the moment of the answer, and it can only have got there from a GRANT a master really sent or a directory reply the cluster really returned. The DIRECTORY node this node's own weight vector resolved is NEVER named as a master — a directory is not a master, and asserting one as master is the fabrication that made a real VAX install OVMX as the master of resources it did not master. There is no code path by which a caller-supplied value reaches the target (the request's own master_csid input is not read on the ENQ path), and the retired OVMX_DLM_ENQ_CSID env crutch has no residual. HONEST RESIDUAL, not papered: this is the ENGINE's decision and its readback. The cat-0x82 reply codec grounds a GRANT shape and a DENY shape only (vms_cluster_codec_dlm.h) — no grounded field carries another node's CSID — and the master/directory-side wire arm (vms_dlm_scs.h's handle_request) is not implemented in kernel-core yet. items.vms: SYSINIT forms or joins the cluster BEFORE the system disk is mounted
items.notes: FC-P0.10/P0.11/P3.9. STARTUP.EXE loads the cluster SYSGEN parameters (VMS_IOCTL_SYSGEN_LOAD), then issues VMS_IOCTL_CLUSTER_START, which starts the fork thread, PEA0:, SCS and the connection manager and forms or joins per VAXCLUSTER -- all of it at boot Step 2d, BEFORE run_startup() and every MOUNT that STARTUP.COM drives. That ordering is the point: a cluster that started from a DCL phase would be a different operating system. VAXCLUSTER=0 issues no ioctl at all (no PEA0:, no HELLO, no console line); =2 with nowhere to join prints VMS's own "waiting to form or join an OpenVMS Cluster" and keeps sweeping; =1 reports STANDALONE. The console line is rendered from the executive's OWN cluster state, read back from struct vms_cluster, never composed from the ioctl's status -- so a JOINING node is never announced as a MEMBER. PROVEN AT R1 (test_cnxman_boot.c pins the step ordering and the state rendering; test_cluster_boot_gate.c the VAXCLUSTER gate) and R4 negctl (tests/qemu/test_cluster_start_negctl.sh). items.vms: Connection Descriptor Table + SCS message/block-transfer service primitives
items.notes: FC-P2.2/P2.4. A pure [state][event] CDT table (ten frozen states, connect/ accept/reject/disconnect half-exchanges, the credit ledger, the SB path-block CDT queue and the VC-break scan) plus vms_scs.c's glue, which binds it DOWN to the port and registers SCS$DIRECTORY. Every send SPENDS a real credit; SCS never retries and never re-opens a connection on its own. PROVEN AT R1/R2/R3, in CI: tests/cluster/host/test_scs_fsm.c, test_scs_fsm_credit.c, test_scs_fsm_vcdown.c, test_scs_glue_conn.c, test_scs_directory.c; the N-node simulator (tests/cluster/sim); tests/qemu/test_cluster_conn.sh drives CLUSTER_DIAG_CONN against a real /dev/vms. NOT claimed: a graded two-node OVMX connection over the wire, or any interoperation with a real VAX — R4-multi-node and R5 are lab-deferred. NEVER-CRASH-A-PEER (vms-5339/#1200+#1202), build-enforced: the whole cluster peer-RECEIVE decode surface -- the DLM body decoders + CM PARAMS + the hello/scs/cm/vc/blk frame codecs (24 decoders; MSCP gate-deferred) -- is fuzzed under ASan/UBSan (~3M inputs total) as a CI gate: no over-read / OOB / UB / crash on any malformed, truncated, or hostile peer frame, and each fuzz asserts dispatch-count>0 (non-vacuity) so a silently-never-reached decoder fails the gate rather than shipping a green facade (INV-6). Locks the never-crash-a-peer invariant as a build-time fact, not an aspiration.

The RECEIVE side is real and reached (scs_fsm_rx_datagram); the frozen scs_sysap_ops has no datagram input routine, so an application datagram is COUNTED rather than delivered -- and deliberately so: wire spec §4(h)(1d) refutes the candidate discriminator between a message and a datagram, and delivering one through the message path would assert a distinction the wire does not carry. An honest, documented partial, not a facade.

Until vms-21b the aux server could not run on a BOOTED distro: TCPIP$INETD.EXE was never staged into the image, and it launched service images by a raw execv of a Linux path (service images are ODS-2-resident at SYS$SYSTEM:, not on the boot initramfs VFS). vms-21b stages it at SYS$SYSTEM: and launches service images the VMS way — materialize off the Files-11 ACP (the shared rms_stage_over_acp DCL RUN + PID1 use) then execve. Both proven by the fail-closed CHECKs in test_syssvc_tcpip_inetd.c and the daytime cold-boot e2e (DAYTIME launches under the low-priv TCPIP$DAYTIME account).
